Definition: to bolt, i.e. figuratively, to flee suddenly
BiblicalUsage: Barach means to flee, to bolt suddenly when danger comes. Hagar flees from Sarai into the wilderness, Moses flees from Pharaoh into Midian, Jonah flees from the presence of the Lord toward Tarshish, and David flees from Saul's house through the window by night.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe fleeing tells the truth about a man's heart, because where he runs shows what he fears and what he trusts. Hagar and Moses fled to the wilderness and found God there, but Jonah fled from God and found a storm, and I hold that the only safe flight is the one that runs toward Him.
